findings.observed: record_server_limitation() requires each call_chain item to have {path,sha256,stage}, then passes the full item to _verify_limitation_reference(). The generic verifier rejects any keys beyond {path,sha256}, so the valid call-chain item is deterministically rejected as not closed.
findings.expected: A structurally valid, hash-bound limitation call chain with the required path, sha256, stage fields and exact stage/order sequence must pass generic reference validation and proceed to the remaining causal and create-once checks.
findings.reproduction: Run the already-preserved exact command and observe FirmwareAcceptanceKitTests.test_server_limitation_create_once_has_causal_and_c3_evidence error with AdmissionError: limitation call chain reference is not closed. The fixture at orchestrator_harness/tests/test_firmware_acceptance_kit.py:135 constructs {path,sha256,stage}; firmware_acceptance/kit.py:434 sends that full object to the exact-key verifier at lines 494-496.
findings.impact: Every valid server-limitation evidence graph is blocked at call-chain admission, so the assigned limitation path cannot create its immutable limitation record or prove its causal pinned-server failure evidence.
findings.no_fix_consequence: The reopened acceptance kit cannot admit an authorized server limitation even when all required evidence is present, preventing reliable certification of the limitation route and keeping the current 20-test shard red.
findings.smallest_fix: Pass a path/sha256-only projection of each call_chain item to the generic verifier while preserving the preceding exact call_chain key, stage, length, and order checks.
findings.complexity: Low: one localized projection at the call-chain verification call.
findings.regression_risk: Low: the exact chain-shape, stage/order, hash, path, identity, predecessor, and downstream evidence checks remain unchanged.
findings.verification_cost: Low: rerun the same two authorized host-only unittest modules after repair; no MCP, server, hardware, or physical resource is required.
findings.alternatives: Changing the call-chain contract to omit stage would weaken the closed ordered evidence graph; weakening the generic verifier would reduce reference integrity for other evidence. A projection preserves both contracts with the smallest surface change.
findings.cost_benefit: The defect is directly demonstrated and blocks every valid limitation admission, while the projection is a narrow code change with low regression and verification cost. Closing this mismatch therefore provides substantially more value than its repair risk and effort.
